item.title: FIFA says it has received more than 500 million ticket requests for 2026 World Cup
item.description: CORAL GABLES, Fla. (AP) — FIFA said Wednesday it has received more than 500 million ticket requests for this year's World Cup.

item.title: Quick quotes: Quebec Premier François Legault announces resignation
item.description: QUÉBEC — Tributes to departing Quebec Premier François Legault started coming in from across the country on Wednesday shortly after the co-founder of the Coalition Avenir Québec party said he would leave office when his replacement is chosen.

item.title: 'Staggering' disparity as Indigenous adults overrepresented in prisons by 10 times
item.description: VANCOUVER — A new report by Statistics Canada says Indigenous adults were incarcerated at a rate 10 times higher than non-Indigenous adults in six provinces, a disparity that justice advocates called staggering, and a roadblock to reconciliation.

item.title: Five topics other than trade that could come up during Carney's China visit
item.description: OTTAWA — Prime Minister Mark Carney is in Beijing this week for meetings with President Xi Jinping and other officials. Upon arriving in China Wednesday, Carney said he was "ready to build a new partnership" with the country.

item.title: Researchers concerned after endangered whooping cranes test positive for bird flu
item.description: SASKATOON — A wildlife biologist says it's deeply concerning that two dead members of a critically endangered flock of birds that only breed in Canadian marshes have tested positive for the avian flu.

item.title: B.C. to end drug decriminalization project, after 'challenging' three-year-experiment

item.title: Alberta government to review Calgary water main breaks, demands documents
item.description: CALGARY — The Alberta government has launched a review of Calgary’s water main ruptures and is demanding the city turn over reams of documents dating back two decades within the next two weeks.

item.title: Federal officer shoots person in leg after being attacked during Minneapolis arrest, officials say
item.description: MINNEAPOLIS (AP) — A federal officer shot a man in the leg in Minneapolis after being attacked with a shovel and broom handle while trying to make an arrest Wednesday, officials said.

item.title: Voting begins in Uganda’s presidential election during internet shutdown and polling station delays
item.description: KAMPALA, Uganda (AP) — Voting began Thursday in Uganda’s presidential election despite a days-long internet shutdown that has been criticized as an anti-democratic gesture in a country where the president has held office since 1986.
